newsitem.title: USA: Coffee prices soar as cold weather threatens Brazil crop.
newsitem.headline: Coffee prices soar as cold weather threatens Brazil crop.

text.p: Coffee prices jumped Tuesday as cold weather approached Brazil's coffee belt, renewing fears of a crop-damaging frost.

Coffee for July delivery closed up 4.10 cents at $1.965 a pound after soaring initially to $2.03, though still well below its record high of $3.18 set in May on the New York Coffee, Sugar and Cocoa Exchange.

A polar air mass posing the greatest frost threat to Brazil's coffee crop so far this year threatens to pass through its major growing areas beginning Saturday night, Brazilian meteorologists predicted.
With the U.S. market closed Friday for the Fourth of July holiday, the cold weather prompted speculators to buy coffee futures contracts in case it proved damaging to crops over the weekend.
But some U.S. weather forecasters said that, although cooler weather was expected, it would not bring crop-damaging frost.
A paralysing strike at one of Brazil's main ports in Santos also lifted coffee prices.
